mainTopic: A כהן and an incomplete body (מת חסר), and the משנה comparing the three prohibitions of a נזיר, tested by a series of קל וחומר arguments
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא that seems to go against רב, who said a כהן does not become טמא for a relative whose body is incomplete. The ברייתא lets a כהן become טמא even for a spine, a skull, or most of the bones. The גמרא answers that this ברייתא follows רבי יהודה. רב follows a different תנא, who tells how the חכמים ruled that 'לאביו' applies only when the father's body is whole. Then a new משנה lists the three things forbidden to a נזיר: טומאה, shaving, and grape products. It explains that each one is stricter than the others in a different way: what cancels days, what has exceptions, and what needs a קרבן. The גמרא then tests every comparison with a קל וחומר. Each time, a פסוק or a practical reason blocks it. For example, shaving cancels days only because the נזיר's hair must grow back, so wine, which leaves the hair in place, cancels nothing.

steps.title: A ברייתא says a כהן becomes impure even for partial remains of any close relative
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from the case of a sister: just as a כהן becomes טמא for her spine, skull, or most of her bones, he becomes טמא for those remains of all his close relatives. This goes against רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think a כהן may not become impure for the spine, the skull, most of the skeleton, or most of the number of bones of his other relatives. You answer: just as his sister is special because her body depends on him, and he becomes impure for her spine, skull, most of her skeleton, or most of her bones, so too for everyone whose body depends on him. He becomes impure for the spine, skull, most of the skeleton, or most of the bones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a ברייתא that lets a כהן become טמא for incomplete remains of any close relative. This is a challenge to רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב had ruled that a כהן does not become טמא for a relative whose head was cut off, because that body is incomplete. This ברייתא says a כהן does become טמא even for only a spine, a skull, or most of the bones. It learns this from the sister to all the other relatives, so it seems to clash with רב.

keyTerms.meaning: Spine
Skull
Most of his skeleton (most of the body's build)
Most of the number of his bones
Her body depends on him (he is the one responsible for her burial)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new statement starting here. It is the end of a ברייתא the גמרא started quoting earlier, and it is being used as a challenge against רב.

phrases.english: One might think he may not become impure
phrases.notes: 'He' is the כהן. A כהן normally may not become טמא to a dead body, except for close relatives.

phrases.english: for a spine or for a skull
or for most of the skeleton or most of the number of bones
of other relatives.
You say: just as his sister is special
in that her body depends on him,
and he becomes impure for the spine and for the skull
and for most of her skeleton and most of her number of bones,
so too anyone whose body depends on him —
he becomes impure for the spine and for the skull
and for most of his skeleton and most of his number of bones.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל לֹא יִטַּמֵּא לַשִּׁדְרָה וְלַגּוּלְגּוֹלֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a ברייתא begun before this section, used against רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that a כהן does not become טמא for a relative whose body is incomplete
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lets a כהן become טמא for partial remains (spine, skull, most of the bones) of any close relative. That means an incomplete body still allows טומאה, against רב.

steps.title: That ברייתא also follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this ברייתא also follows רבי יהודה, so רב does not have to agree with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: That ברייתא, too, follows רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by saying the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'also' shows that an earlier source was already explained as רבי יהודה's view. Since this ברייתא is just one תנא's view, רב can follow a different תנא.

keyTerms.meaning: That one (that ברייתא)
Also

phrases.english: That one, too, is the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהִיא נָמֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the challenging source to a specific תנא (רבי יהודה) whom רב need not follow
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to be an accepted ruling that disproves רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is רבי יהודה's view only. רב holds like a different תנא.

steps.title: רב follows a תנא who tells the story of רבי יצחק's father
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows which תנא רב follows. It quotes a ברייתא about רבי יצחק, whose father died in גינזק. He was told only three years later, and he asked the חכמים what to do.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said his ruling like this תנא, as a ברייתא teaches: It happened that the father of רבי יצחק died in גינזק. People came and told him after three years. He came and asked רבי יהושע בן אלישע and the four elders with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source for רב's view and sets up a story. The ruling of the חכמים comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After saying the opposing ברייתא is רבי יהודה's view, the גמרא shows that רב is not alone. The key detail is the three years: by then the father's body would no longer be whole. That sets up the question of whether a כהן may become טמא for an incomplete body.

keyTerms.meaning: Like this תנא
An incident, a story that happened
They informed him
Elders, the חכמים

phrases.english: And Rav said his ruling like this tanna,
as it is taught in a baraita:
An incident in which the father died
of Rabbi Yitzchak, in Ginzak,
phrases.notes: גינזק is the name of a place. רבי יצחק was a כהן.

phrases.english: and they came and informed him
after three years,

phrases.aramaic: וּבָא וְשָׁאַל אֶת רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן אֱלִישָׁע
phrases.english: and he came and asked Rabbi Yehoshua ben Elisha
and four elders [who were with him],
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are added in the corrected wording.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב דְּאָמַר כִּי הַאי תַּנָּא דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the positive source for רב after step 2 removed the challenge.
steps.raayaObject: רב's ruling that a כהן does not become טמא for an incomplete body
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording a ruling given to רבי יצחק by רבי יהושע בן אלישע and four elders

steps.title: 'For his father' only when the body is whole
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ruled from the word 'לאביו' that a כהן becomes טמא for his father only when the body is whole, not when it is lacking. This matches רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: 'For his father' means when he is whole, and not when he is lacking.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים give their answer: the permission for a כהן to become טמא applies only to a whole body. This is the support for רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'לאביו', 'for his father'. The חכמים read this as the father in his complete form. After three years the body was no longer whole, so רבי יצחק could not become טמא. That is just like רב's case of a relative whose head was cut off.

keyTerms.meaning: Whole, complete
Lacking, incomplete
'For his father', from the פסוק that allows a כהן to become טמא for relatives

steps.whatToRemember: רב holds like the תנא of this story: a כהן becomes טמא for a relative only when the body is whole (not מת חסר). The ברייתא allowing partial remains follows רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: And they said: 'For his father' —
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:2

phrases.english: when he is whole,
and not when he is lacking.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמְרוּ לְאָבִיו בִּזְמַן שֶׁהוּא שָׁלֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ruling in the story set up in step 3.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A כהן becomes טמא for his relative only when the body is whole. This supports רב.

steps.title: New משנה: three things forbidden to a נזיר
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה lists the three categories forbidden to a נזיר: טומאה, shaving, and anything that comes from the grapevine.
steps.simpleTranslation: Three types of things are forbidden to a נזיר: impurity, shaving, and whatever comes from the grapevine.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins and lists the three basic prohibitions of a נזיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This moves from the topic of a כהן's טומאה to the general structure of נזירות. The three categories are named here so the משנה can compare them in the next line.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (start of a new משנה)
Someone who took a vow of נזירות
Ritual impurity (here from a dead body)
Shaving the hair
Whatever comes from the grapevine (wine, grapes, and the like)

phrases.english: MISHNA: Three types are forbidden to a nazirite:
impurity, and shaving,
and what comes from the vine.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלֹשָׁה מִינִין אֲסוּרִין בַּנָּזִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. The previous topic has ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נזיר is forbidden in three things: טומאה, shaving, and products of the grapevine.

steps.title: Impurity and shaving are stricter than grape products
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says טומאה and shaving are stricter than grape products, because they cancel days of נזירות already kept, while grape products do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Impurity and shaving are stricter than what comes from the vine. Impurity and shaving cancel his counted days, but what comes from the vine does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה compares the three prohibitions and explains why two of them are stricter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three are forbidden, but breaking them has different results. טומאה and shaving 'knock down' the days of נזירות he already kept, so he must make some up. Eating or drinking grape products is a sin, but the days he counted still stand.

keyTerms.meaning: A stricter point
They cancel, knocking down days already counted

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the framework the coming סוגיא will analyze: which prohibitions cancel the counted days of נזירות and which do not.

phrases.english: There is a greater strictness with impurity and shaving
than with what comes from the vine,
for impurity and shaving cancel,
phrases.notes: Literally 'tear down': they knock down days of נזירות he already kept, so he has to make some up.

phrases.english: but what comes from the vine does not cancel.

steps.triggerLanguage: חוֹמֶר בַּטּוּמְאָה וּבַתִּגְלַחַת מִבַּיּוֹצֵא מִן הַגֶּפֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the three prohibitions listed in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: טומאה and shaving cancel counted days of נזירות. Grape products do not.

steps.title: Grape products are stricter: they have no exceptions
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says that grape products are stricter than טומאה and shaving in one way: they are never allowed, while טומאה and shaving are allowed in special מצוה cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: Grape products are stricter than טומאה and shaving, because grape products are never allowed. טומאה and shaving are allowed in certain cases: shaving that is a מצוה, and a מת מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now turns the comparison around. It shows one way in which grape products are actually stricter than the other two prohibitions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 6, טומאה and shaving were stricter because they cancel days already kept. Here we learn the other side: grape products have no exceptions at all, while טומאה and shaving each have a case where the Torah allows them. So each prohibition is stricter in its own way.

keyTerms.meaning: A stricter side; a way in which one law is more severe than another
Anything that comes from the grapevine (wine, grapes, and so on)
Was allowed out of its general rule; it has an exception
Shaving that is required as a מצוה
A dead body with no one else to bury it

steps.confusionAlert: Step 6 said טומאה and shaving are stricter, and now the משנה says grape products are stricter. Both are true. Each prohibition is stricter in a different way.

phrases.english: There is a stricter side to what comes from the vine
than to impurity and shaving,
because what comes from the vine
was never allowed out of its general rule,
phrases.notes: In other words, there is no case where a נזיר may have grape products.

phrases.english: but impurity and shaving were allowed out of their general rule
in mitzvah-shaving and with a מת מצוה.
phrases.notes: A מת מצוה is a dead body that nobody else will bury, so even a נזיר must bury it.

steps.triggerLanguage: חוֹמֶר בַּיּוֹצֵא מִן הַגֶּפֶן מִבַּטּוּמְאָה וּבַתִּגְלַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The flip side of step 6: now grape products are shown to be stricter in a different way.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Grape products have no exceptions. טומאה and shaving have exceptions: תגלחת מצוה and מת מצוה.

steps.title: Impurity is stricter than shaving
steps.stepSummary: The משנה compares טומאה to shaving. טומאה cancels all the days and needs a קרבן. Shaving cancels only thirty days and needs no קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: טומאה is stricter than shaving. טומאה cancels all the days already kept, and the נזיר must bring a קרבן for it. Shaving cancels only thirty days, and no קרבן is needed for it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its comparison by ranking the two stricter prohibitions, טומאה and shaving, against each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both of them cancel days, but not to the same degree. טומאה wipes out the whole נזירות so far, and it also needs a קרבן. Shaving cancels at most thirty days and has no קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: Cancels; knocks down the days of נזירות already kept
All of it, meaning every day kept so far
One must bring a sacrifice for it
Thirty days

steps.whatToRemember: The full ranking: grape products have no exceptions. טומאה and shaving cancel days. Of those two, טומאה is stricter, because it cancels everything and needs a קרבן.

phrases.english: And there is a stricter side to impurity than to shaving,
because impurity cancels everything,
and one must bring an offering for it.
But shaving cancels only thirty,
phrases.notes: Thirty days of the נזירות at most, not the whole thing.

phrases.english: and one does not have to bring an offering for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחוֹמֶר בַּטּוּמְאָה מִבַּתִּגְלַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה's comparison by ranking טומאה against shaving.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: טומאה cancels all the days and needs a קרבן. Shaving cancels only thirty days and needs no קרבן.

steps.title: A קל וחומר says impurity should have no exception
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה's exception for מת מצוה. If יין, which does not cancel days, has no exceptions, then surely טומאה, which does cancel days, should have none either.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe טומאה should not be allowed even for a מת מצוה, because of a קל וחומר from יין. יין does not cancel days, and still it has no exception. טומאה does cancel days, so isn't it logical that it should have no exception either?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and challenges the משנה's statement that a נזיר may become טמא for a מת מצוה. It uses a קל וחומר from יין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument uses step 6: טומאה is stricter than יין because it cancels days. If the lighter one (יין) has no exception, the stricter one (טומאה) should have none either. That would make the משנה's exception for מת מצוה wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for גמרא; the discussion of the משנה starts here
A logical argument: if the lighter case is strict, the stricter case surely is
'And if...': the opening word of a קל וחומר
Isn't it logical? (the closing words of a קל וחומר)

phrases.english: GEMARA:
But let impurity not be allowed out of its general rule,
by a קל וחומר from wine:
And if wine, which does not cancel,
phrases.notes: It does not cancel the days of נזירות already kept, as the משנה said in step 6.

phrases.english: was not allowed out of its general rule,
then impurity, which does cancel,
isn't it logical that it should not be allowed out of its general rule?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְטוּמְאָה לֹא תּוּתַּר מִכְּלָלָהּ, קַל וָחוֹמֶר מִיַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the exception for מת מצוה from step 7, using the 'cancels days' point from step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that טומאה is allowed for a מת מצוה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר: יין is lighter (it does not cancel days) and has no exception, so טומאה, which is stricter, should have no exception either.

steps.title: The verse allows impurity for a מת מצוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers from the פסוק 'לאביו ולאמו לא יטמא'. A נזיר may not become טמא for his father and mother, but he does become טמא for a מת מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'For his father and for his mother he shall not become impure.' For his father and mother he may not become impure, but he does become impure for a מת מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the קל וחומר. A פסוק teaches the exception directly, so logic cannot cancel it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah already said in general that a נזיר may not go near a dead body. So naming father and mother is read to mean: only for relatives like these is he forbidden, but for a מת מצוה he becomes טמא. When a פסוק says something clearly, a קל וחומר cannot override it.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches; it introduces a proof from a פסוק
He shall not become impure
He does become impure

steps.whatToRemember: A נזיר may not become טמא even for his own father and mother, but he must become טמא to bury a מת מצוה. The source is a פסוק, so the קל וחומר from יין is rejected.

phrases.english: The verse states:
"For his father or for his mother he shall not become impure."
phrases.notes: במדבר 6:7

phrases.english: For his father and his mother he may not become impure,
but he does become impure for a מת מצוה.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קל וחומר of step 9 with a direct reading of a פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Scriptural derivation that overrides a logical argument
steps.terutzHavaAmina: By the קל וחומר from יין, טומאה should have no exception at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק limits the prohibition to relatives such as father and mother, so a נזיר does become טמא for a מת מצוה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the משנה's rule that a נזיר must become טמא to bury a מת מצוה. It also shows that a קל וחומר gives way when a פסוק teaches otherwise.

steps.title: Why not allow wine for a מצוה too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues with a קל וחומר: if טומאה, which is stricter, has a מצוה exception, then יין, which is more lenient, should have one too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let wine also be allowed in a special case, by a קל וחומר from טומאה. טומאה cancels the days, and yet it is allowed in a special case. Wine does not cancel the days, so surely it should be allowed in a special case too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the argument from Step 9 around. Since טומאה has a מצוה exception, it asks why יין should not have one as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 showed from a פסוק that טומאה is allowed for a מת מצוה. Now the גמרא reasons: טומאה is the stricter one, because it cancels days. If even the stricter one has an exception, the more lenient one (יין) should surely have an exception too, for a מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: Permitted out of its general rule, meaning allowed in a special case
An argument from a lighter case to a stricter case, or the reverse
Cancels (the days of נזירות already kept)
Is it not logical?

phrases.english: And let wine be permitted out of its general rule,
phrases.notes: This means that wine would be allowed in a special מצוה case, the way טומאה is allowed for a מת מצוה.

phrases.english: by a קל וחומר from impurity:
If impurity, which cancels the days,
is permitted out of its general rule,
then wine, which does not cancel the days,
is it not logical that it should be permitted out of its general rule?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיַיִן יוּתַּר מִכְּלָלוֹ, קַל וָחוֹמֶר מִטּוּמְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the מצוה exception for טומאה, just proven in Step 10, to argue for a similar exception for יין.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule in the משנה that grape products are never permitted (Step 7).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר: if the stricter prohibition (טומאה, which cancels days) has an exception, the more lenient one (יין) should surely have one too.

steps.title: מצוה wine is forbidden like ordinary wine
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק teaches that even wine for a מצוה is forbidden to a נזיר, so the קל וחומר does not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'From wine and strong drink he shall abstain.' This comes to forbid מצוה wine just like ordinary wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק showing that wine has no מצוה exception at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר made sense on its own. But the פסוק goes against it and teaches that wine drunk for a מצוה is treated exactly like wine drunk by choice. When a פסוק says something different, the קל וחומר does not stand.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק says
He shall abstain
Wine drunk for a מצוה
Wine drunk by choice (ordinary wine)

phrases.english: The verse says:
"From wine and strong drink he shall abstain,"
phrases.notes: במדבר 6:3

phrases.english: to forbid מצוה wine like optional wine.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: ״מִיַּיִן וְשֵׁכָר יַזִּיר״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קל וחומר of Step 11 by pointing to a פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Scriptural source overrides the logical inference
steps.terutzHavaAmina: By קל וחומר‎, מצוה wine should be permitted to a נזיר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק forbids מצוה wine exactly like ordinary wine.
steps.whyThisMatters: This confirms the משנה in Step 7: grape products have no exceptions at all.

steps.title: Why not let wine cancel all the days?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא makes a new קל וחומר: wine has no exceptions, which makes it stricter, so it should cancel all the days like טומאה does.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let wine cancel all the days, by a קל וחומר from טומאה. טומאה is allowed in a special case, and yet it cancels everything. Wine is never allowed, so surely it should cancel everything!
steps.whatsHappening: Now that wine has turned out to be stricter in one way (no exceptions), the גמרא uses that to ask why wine should not also cancel all the days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the strictness runs the other way. Wine is stricter because it is never allowed. If טומאה, which is more lenient in that way, cancels all the days, then wine should surely cancel all the days too.

keyTerms.meaning: It should cancel everything (all the days kept)

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Wine is stricter than טומאה because it has no exceptions. So it should share טומאה's harsh result of cancelling all the days.

steps.title: Only טומאה cancels the days
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק teaches that the days are cancelled because of טומאה, and wine does not cancel them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And the first days shall fall away, because his נזירות became impure.' This teaches that טומאה cancels the days, but wine does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא again answers with a פסוק, showing that cancelling days belongs only to טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links the falling away of the days to טומאה specifically ('because his נזירות became impure'). That limits the rule of cancelling the days to טומאה alone. So the קל וחומר for wine is blocked.

steps.title: Why shouldn't shaving cancel all the days?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that shaving is stricter than טומאה in one way, so it should cancel all the days, not just thirty.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let shaving cancel all the days, by a קל וחומר from טומאה. With טומאה, the person who makes the נזיר impure is not treated like the נזיר who becomes impure, and yet טומאה cancels everything. With shaving, the person who shaves the נזיר is treated like the נזיר who is shaved. Is it not logical that shaving should cancel everything?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now attacks the משנה's rule (Step 8) that shaving cancels only thirty days. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With shaving, even the person who shaves a נזיר is held responsible, just like the נזיר himself. That makes shaving look stricter than טומאה, where only the נזיר is responsible. So the גמרא asks why shaving should not cancel all the days, the way טומאה does.

steps.title: Should someone who makes a נזיר impure be treated like the נזיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues with a קל וחומר: since someone who shaves a נזיר is treated like the נזיר who was shaved, someone who makes a נזיר impure should be treated like the נזיר who became impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: And with impurity, let us treat the one who makes a נזיר impure like the one who becomes impure, through a קל וחומר from shaving. Shaving cancels only thirty days, and still the one who shaves is treated like the one who is shaved. Impurity cancels everything, so isn't it logical that the one who makes impure should be treated like the one who becomes impure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns the comparison around. Since טומאה is stricter in that it cancels all the days, it should also have the rule that shaving has: the person who causes it is treated like the נזיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With shaving, the person who shaves a נזיר is held responsible just like the נזיר himself (מגלח כמתגלח). Shaving is the more lenient one, because it cancels only thirty days. So the גמרא argues that טומאה, the stricter one, should certainly have the same rule: מטמא כמיטמא.

steps.title: A verse limits impurity to the נזיר himself
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'and he makes impure the head of his נזירות' teaches that the טומאה prohibition applies only to the נזיר who makes his own head impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: "And he makes impure the head of his נזירות." This teaches that the law is only for the נזיר who makes his own head impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks the קל וחומר of step 17 with a פסוק. The טומאה prohibition is only on the נזיר himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks about the person who 'makes impure the head of his נזירות', meaning the נזיר's own head. That shows the Torah is talking only about the נזיר himself, not about someone else who brought impurity onto him. So there is no מטמא כמיטמא, even though logic seemed to call for it.

steps.title: Maybe shaving should not have this rule either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reverses the argument: if טומאה, which is stricter, has no מטמא כמיטמא, then shaving, which is more lenient, should not have מגלח כמתגלח.
steps.simpleTranslation: And with shaving, let us not treat the one who shaves like the one who is shaved, through a קל וחומר from impurity. Impurity cancels everything, and still the one who makes impure is not treated like the one who becomes impure. Shaving cancels only thirty days, so all the more so the one who shaves should not be treated like the one who is shaved!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes the result of step 18 and uses it against shaving. If the stricter case lacks this rule, the more lenient case should surely lack it too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 showed that טומאה has no מטמא כמיטמא. Since טומאה is stricter because it cancels everything, the גמרא now argues with a קל וחומר that shaving, which cancels only 30 days, should not have מגלח כמתגלח either. This attacks a rule that was assumed as the starting point of step 17, and the גמרא will need to answer it.

steps.title: The verse forbids another person from shaving a נזיר too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge against מגלח כמתגלח. It reads the פסוק 'תער לא יעבור על ראשו' as also forbidding a person from shaving someone else who is a נזיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'No razor shall pass over his head.' Read it as: he shall not pass a razor over himself, and another person shall not pass a razor over him.
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge in Step 19 said that shaving should not have the rule of מגלח כמתגלח. The גמרא answers that the rule does not come from logic. It comes straight from the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר in Step 19 would have cancelled the rule that the one who shaves a נזיר is also punished. But a קל וחומר cannot override a פסוק. By reading 'לא יעבור' as 'לא יעביר' (he shall not cause to pass), the פסוק includes both the נזיר and anyone who shaves a נזיר.

steps.title: Why should shaving ever be permitted, when wine never is?
steps.stepSummary: A קל וחומר from wine: wine does not cancel days, and it is never permitted. Shaving does cancel days, so it should never be permitted either.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shaving should not be permitted out of its general rule, by a קל וחומר from wine. Wine does not cancel the days, and it is not permitted out of its general rule. Shaving does cancel the days. Is it not logical that it should not be permitted out of its general rule?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new challenge. It asks why a נזיר who is a מצורע is allowed to shave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wine is a 'lighter' נזיר prohibition because it does not cancel any days, yet it never has an exception. Shaving is 'heavier' because it cancels days. So it seems that shaving should have no exception at all, even for a מצורע.

steps.stepSummary: The פסוק about the מצורע says he shaves 'his head' and 'his beard'. This shows that he shaves even if he is a נזיר.

steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra words 'ראשו' and 'זקנו' in the מצורע section show that the Torah wants the shaving done even where it is otherwise forbidden, such as for a נזיר. Since the exception is written in a פסוק, the קל וחומר from wine does not apply.

steps.title: Then shaving should not cancel any days at all
steps.stepSummary: A reverse קל וחומר: wine has no exception and still does not cancel days. Shaving has an exception, so it should not cancel days either.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shaving should not cancel at all, by a קל וחומר from wine. Wine is not permitted out of its general rule, and it does not cancel. Shaving is permitted out of its general rule. Is it not logical that it should not cancel?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא turns the comparison around. It uses the exception for shaving to argue that shaving is the lighter one, so it should not cancel days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 21, shaving looked stricter because it cancels days. Now shaving looks lighter because it has an exception (the מצורע). Wine looks stricter because it has no exception. Since even wine does not cancel days, shaving should not cancel days either.

steps.title: Shaving cancels days because the hair must grow back
steps.stepSummary: Shaving cancels days for a practical reason: the נזיר needs grown hair, and after shaving he has none.
steps.simpleTranslation: We need hair growth, and here there is none.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the קל וחומר does not matter here. Shaving cancels days because the נזיר's hair is gone and must grow back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Shaving does not cancel days because it is a 'strict' sin. It cancels days because a נזיר needs a full growth of hair during his נזירות, and after shaving there is no hair. So a comparison of strictness with wine does not apply.

steps.title: Then wine should cancel thirty days
steps.stepSummary: Another קל וחומר: shaving has an exception and still cancels days. Wine has no exception, so it should cancel thirty days too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Wine should cancel thirty days, by a קל וחומר from shaving. Shaving is permitted out of its general rule, yet it cancels. Wine is not permitted out of its general rule. Is it not logical that it should cancel?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes one more comparison. It asks why drinking wine does not cancel thirty days, the same as shaving does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Shaving is the lighter one, since it has an exception, and it still cancels thirty days. Wine is the stricter one, since it has no exception. So wine should cancel at least as much as shaving.

If shaving, which was permitted out of its general rule —

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיַיִן יִסְתּוֹר שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם, קַל וָחוֹמֶר מִתִּגְלַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that shaving is shown to cancel days, the גמרא asks whether wine should cancel days too.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that wine does not cancel any days
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קל וחומר: the lighter prohibition (shaving) cancels thirty days, so the stricter one (wine) should cancel them too.

steps.title: With wine, the hair is still there
steps.stepSummary: The only reason shaving cancels days is hair growth. With wine the hair is still in place, so there is nothing to make up.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is the reason anything other than hair growth? With wine, his hair is still standing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with the same idea as Step 24. Shaving cancels days only because the hair is gone. Wine does not remove any hair, so it cancels nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once we know that shaving cancels days only because of hair growth, every strictness comparison with wine falls away. Drinking wine is forbidden, but it does not change the נזיר's hair, so no days need to be added.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it anything (other than)?
Reason
Stands; remains in place

steps.whatToRemember: A קל וחומר cannot override a פסוק. The פסוקים teach מגלח כמתגלח and the מצורע's shaving. Shaving cancels thirty days only because the נזיר's hair must grow back, so wine, which leaves the hair in place, cancels nothing.
steps.whyThisMatters: This one practical reason, hair growth, explains why only shaving cancels days. That is why the strictness comparisons with wine fail in both directions.
